Case Facts: Smith v. Jones is a landmark ruling where the plaintiff, Smith, accused Jones of breach of contract. Smith claimed Jones failed to honor a handshake agreement promising a 25% share of profits from a joint business venture. Although there was no written agreement, Smith provided witnesses who confirmed the existence of the agreement and its terms.

Legal Points: The case addresses the enforceability of oral or handshake agreements in contract law, specifically highlighting that witness testimony can substantiate the existence and terms of an agreement even in the absence of a written document.
